``` ::: ::: For imidacloprid, the lowest BIC was obtained for the model combining effects on maintenance and growth (BIC = -65.1; @tbl-IMDTKTDres). However, the assimilation-and-growth formulation received nearly equivalent support (BIC = -64.1; $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=1.0$), whereas the growth-and-reproduction model was less supported (BIC = -62.8; $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=2.3$). The remaining formulations showed substantially higher BIC values. These results therefore did not allow a clear statistical distinction between the maintenance-and-growth and assimilation-and-growth pMoAs. Because imidacloprid is known to affect earthworm activity, feeding behaviour, and bioturbation [@dittbrenner_2010], a reduction in resource acquisition or processing was considered biologically more plausible than a primary increase in maintenance costs. The assimilation-and-growth formulation was therefore retained for subsequent analyses, while acknowledging the maintenance-and-growth model as an equally plausible statistical alternative. The selected assimilation and growth model estimated a no-effect concentration ($c_0$) of 1,132 \[882; 1,494\] ng$\cdot$g$^{-1}$ internal concentration and a stress slope parameter ($b$) of 0.02 \[0.01; 8.54\] g$\cdot$ng$^{-1}$. The wide credible interval around $b$ indicates that the increase in stress above the threshold remained poorly constrained. ## Chains ::: panel-tabset ## A ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Parameters chains. model captured the main concentration-response patterns observed for juvenile growth, adult growth, and reproduction (@fig-pred_F_IMD_AGsummary & @fig-predobs_F_IMD_AG). It reproduced the general decline in life-history performance with increasing imidacloprid exposure, supporting a physiological mode of action involving both reduced assimilation and altered growth processes. Nevertheless, some systematic deviations remained across the exposure gradient. ``` ::: ::: Predicted internal concentrations increased throughout the 28-day exposure at the four lowest imidacloprid concentrations, with maximum values reached at the end of the experiment (@fig-pred_F_IMD_AG_summary_Ciarticle, @tbl-CirecapIMD). From 0.16 mg$\cdot$kg$^{-1}$ onwards, internal concentrations reached the estimated saturation level of 1,676 ng$\cdot$g$^{-1}$, with the time required to reach this plateau decreasing as external concentration increased. Consequently, the highest exposure treatments differed mainly in how rapidly the saturation level was reached rather than in their maximal internal concentration. Predicted concentrations were slightly higher in adults than in juveniles at the lower exposure levels, but both life stages converged towards the same saturation plateau. The estimated no-effect concentration of 1,132 ng$\cdot$g$^{-1}$ was exceeded only from 0.16 mg$\cdot$kg$^{-1}$ onwards, corresponding to the concentration range in which toxic effects were predicted to emerge.
